why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 only tests that clamp is exported as a function and that sample values (including the boundaries and decimals) come back "limited to [lo, hi]". That is what the words require. Check 2 only tests that a RangeError is thrown for three cases where lo > hi. Check 3 requires each exported function to have a README entry that "names it and describes what it does". That is a fair reading of "documents"; the hard-coded list of names is only a note. Check 4 only requires "fail 0 and exits 0". The stricter items sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)": that lo===hi doesn't throw, how clear the error message is, that tests exist, and the README style and RangeError mention. No PASS or FAIL condition has a test, mutation, branch or file-scope rule, or exact-wording rule beyond what the words require.
